metric_rationale: Calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic. Because the experiment is carefully designed such that TTB and Tallying make opposing predictions on most trials, this single metric will yield a high value (~0.9) for TTB-simulated data and a low value (~0.1) for Tallying-simulated data, robustly discriminating the two theories with very low between-subject variance.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that are consistent with the Tallying heuristic on trials where Tallying makes a deterministic prediction (i.e., one option has strictly more winning features than the other). By experimental design (trials 1-4), Tallying and Take The Best (TTB) make perfectly opposite predictions on these trials. Tallying chooses the option with more winning features, while TTB chooses the other option because it wins on the single highest-validity cue. Therefore, data generated by Tallying will score very high on this metric (near 1.0, minus noise), while data generated by TTB will score very low (near 0.0, plus noise). This massive difference in means, combined with stable within-subject measurement over 64 such trials, provides excellent discriminability.
